task:

The target branch already contains one owner-verified commit with three files you must use unchanged: scripts/operator/octopus-upgrade/package.json, scripts/operator/octopus-upgrade/package-lock.json (pinned Prisma CLI 7.5.0 + dotenv 17.4.2) and scripts/operator/octopus-upgrade/openai-models.sql (idempotent INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ("modelId") DO NOTHING of 10 OpenAI model rows). Their SHA-256: package.json fe6e369eac296a68d283576f484093f6a0213fc77cf97998d79463d07f1f0d5e, package-lock.json 871e50428cfae28914c7d871b8a70f9b0cd27704ac47d3ff9216c9ec92694ba0, openai-models.sql bbf4daa73643b00f1b979b43f0950ffda5357e24ff84dff766053646fcdd70d3. Do not edit them.

Facts about production (read by the owner on the host on 2026-10-31; do not re-derive):
- Host `ed-finder-prod`; Octopus lives in `/opt/octopus`, a git checkout of https://github.com/octopusreview/octopus at tag v1.0.122 (commit 55583ac832472ad8b535f1f678f9c11837f7cfdb). `git status` shows only the known local change to docker-compose.selfhost.yml (the qdrant healthcheck repair) and its backup file.
- Compose file `/opt/octopus/docker-compose.selfhost.yml`; containers `octopus-web-1` (ghcr.io/octopusreview/octopus-selfhost:1.0.122), `octopus-postgres-1` (postgres:17-alpine), `octopus-qdrant-1` (qdrant/qdrant:v1.17.0). The web image line is `ghcr.io/octopusreview/octopus-selfhost:${OCTOPUS_VERSION:-latest}`; `/opt/octopus/.env` contains exactly one line `OCTOPUS_VERSION=1.0.122`. The compose `web` service sets `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://octopus:octopus@postgres:5432/octopus` (public compose default, not a secret).
- Octopus database: 20 MB; `_prisma_migrations` has 35 finished, 0 failed, newest `20260813200000_retire_opus_4647_reorder_models` (exactly v1.0.122's 35 migrations).
- 242 GB free on /. The host reaches registry.npmjs.org.

The procedure below was rehearsed end to end by the owner's operator in a disposable copy (1.0.122 database with data -> stage 1 -> 1.0.122 still healthy -> image 1.3.3 healthy -> stage 2 -> models; and pg_restore of the pre-upgrade dump back to a working 1.0.122). Implement exactly this procedure.

PINNED CONSTANTS (in the action, never from caller input):
- FROM_VERSION=1.0.122, FROM_COMMIT=55583ac832472ad8b535f1f678f9c11837f7cfdb, FROM_IMAGE_DIGEST=sha256:7a65a6009136376a74ff0a4dd58fae26c10f610879bed7f9c97adb0530c7eb78
- TO_VERSION=1.3.3, TO_COMMIT=634c32d71f06576e5e71ee2895d694668fd15a7a, TO_IMAGE=ghcr.io/octopusreview/octopus-selfhost:1.3.3, TO_IMAGE_DIGEST=sha256:dd36e9e7b9a8c092cf4382c1129500aa776e0848d72f28e45fdb5ac3e53fd043
- MIGRATOR_IMAGE=ghcr.io/brianstewart377-rgb/ed-finder/mirror/node@sha256:e67514e5d0f6c46656005e1b693b2ec9d52e80b641307de684d4a015ba7a4eaf (the repo's own pinned node:24-alpine mirror, already listed in .github/ci-image-mirror.txt)
- OCTOPUS_REMOTE=https://github.com/octopusreview/octopus
- EXPECTED migration counts: 35 before, 60 after stage 1, 61 after stage 2; the one migration held back from stage 1 is `20260929150000_sonnet55` (Octopus's upgrade notes say its catalog row must land only after compatible code runs).
- The three committed file SHA-256 values above.

1. scripts/operator/actions/octopus-upgrade.sh — one script, mode given as the first argument by the workflow (`preflight` or `apply`, nothing else accepted). Follow scripts/operator/actions/octopus-qdrant-healthcheck-repair.sh closely for style and guards: `set -euo pipefail`; CPython 3.14 check; JSON receipt with schema_version "ed-finder/operator-operation-result/v1" and operation "octopus-upgrade-preflight" / "octopus-upgrade-apply"; host must be `ed-finder-prod`; root; cwd `/opt/ed-finder`; `/opt/octopus`, the compose file and `.env` present; docker and docker compose present. Never `set -x`, never print `.env` contents, never print rendered compose values other than the three image references; compare `DATABASE_URL` without printing it.
   The committed package.json, package-lock.json and openai-models.sql reach the host through the streamed script (see workflow step); before use, the action writes them to a fresh `mktemp -d` work directory (mode 700) and verifies each SHA-256 against the pinned constants, stopping on any mismatch.

   PREFLIGHT (read-only; must not pull images, write files outside its mktemp dir, or change containers/DB). Report as JSON:
   - purge fence result from `v3_purge_state_check` (report only; preflight does not refuse on it);
   - rendered images of web/postgres/qdrant; running web container image digest; whether `/opt/octopus/.env` has exactly one `OCTOPUS_VERSION=` line and whether its value is 1.0.122 or 1.3.3 (value only, never other lines);
   - `git -C /opt/octopus rev-parse HEAD` vs FROM_COMMIT, origin URL vs OCTOPUS_REMOTE, and `git status --porcelain` file names (names only);
   - `_prisma_migrations` counts (finished/not-finished-or-rolled-back) and max migration_name, via `docker exec octopus-postgres-1 psql -U octopus -d octopus -tAc ...`;
   - active Octopus background jobs: `select count(*) from pgboss.job where state='active'` (report null if the table is absent);
   - web `/api/version` read inside the container: `docker exec octopus-web-1 node -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/version').then(r=>r.text()).then(t=>console.log(t))"`;
   - free bytes on the filesystem holding /var/lib/docker and /opt/octopus;
   - a verdict: `ready` (everything matches the 1.0.122 facts above), `already_upgraded` (rendered + running web on 1.3.3 digest, 61 finished migrations, all 10 OpenAI rows present), or `blocked` with machine-readable reasons.

   APPLY (manual dispatch on main only; purge-fenced). Steps, in order:
   a. All preflight checks must give `ready` (or exit 0 with status `already_done` when `already_upgraded`, changing nothing). Refuse if `v3_purge_state_check` refuses, if active pgboss jobs > 0, if free space < 10 GiB, or if anything differs from the facts above.
   b. `docker pull TO_IMAGE` and require `docker image inspect` RepoDigests to contain `ghcr.io/octopusreview/octopus-selfhost@TO_IMAGE_DIGEST`; `docker pull MIGRATOR_IMAGE`. Stop (nothing changed) on failure.
   c. Source for migrations: `git -C /opt/octopus fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin TO_COMMIT`, require `git -C /opt/octopus rev-parse TO_COMMIT^{commit}` == TO_COMMIT, then `git -C /opt/octopus archive TO_COMMIT packages/db/prisma packages/db/prisma.config.ts` extracted twice into the work dir as `stage1/` and `stage2/`; delete `stage1/packages/db/prisma/migrations/20260929150000_sonnet55`; require 60 and 61 migration directories respectively; copy the verified package.json and package-lock.json into the root of both. Do NOT check out anything in /opt/octopus (the working tree and its local compose change must stay untouched).
   d. Backup (point of no return starts after this): create `/opt/octopus/backups` (mode 700) and write `docker exec octopus-postgres-1 pg_dump -U octopus -d octopus -Fc` to `/opt/octopus/backups/octopus-before-1.3.3-<UTC timestamp>.dump` (mode 600); verify it with `docker exec -i octopus-postgres-1 pg_restore --list < dump` listing at least one TABLE entry. Copy `/opt/octopus/.env` to `/opt/octopus/backups/env-before-1.3.3-<timestamp>` preserving mode and owner.
   e. Stage 1: run the migrator container on the Octopus postgres container's single Docker network (discover it with `docker inspect`; stop unless exactly one), mounting `stage1` at /work: `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund && cd packages/db && ../../node_modules/.bin/prisma migrate deploy` with `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://octopus:octopus@postgres:5432/octopus`, `--rm`, no host mounts other than the work dir, no `--network host`, no privileged flags. Then require 60 finished / 0 failed migrations and the old web still answering version 1.0.122.
   f. Switch the image: atomically replace the single `OCTOPUS_VERSION=1.0.122` line in /opt/octopus/.env with `OCTOPUS_VERSION=1.3.3` (temp file in /opt/octopus, same mode/owner, `mv`), change nothing else in the file; then `docker compose --project-directory /opt/octopus -f /opt/octopus/docker-compose.selfhost.yml up -d --no-deps web`; require the running web container's image to resolve to TO_IMAGE_DIGEST and `/api/version` to report 1.3.3 within 180 seconds.
   g. Stage 2: same migrator run with `stage2`; require 61 finished / 0 failed.
   h. Models: `docker exec -i octopus-postgres-1 psql -U octopus -d octopus -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q < openai-models.sql`, then require all 10 modelIds from that file to exist with provider 'openai' and category 'llm', and `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-sonnet-5-5` rows to exist.
   i. Final check: web version 1.3.3 and healthy; receipt status `passed` with the backup paths, migration counts before/after, image digests before/after, model rows added.
   ROLLBACK: if any step from (e) onward fails, automatically: restore `.env` from the backup copy if it was changed; `docker compose ... stop web`; `psql -U octopus -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c 'DROP DATABASE octopus WITH (FORCE)' -c 'CREATE DATABASE octopus OWNER octopus'`; `docker exec -i octopus-postgres-1 pg_restore -U octopus -d octopus --no-owner < dump`; require 35 finished migrations; `docker compose ... up -d --no-deps web`; require version 1.0.122 within 180 s. Receipt status `rolled_back` (or `rollback_failed`, naming the step) with the original failure reason; exit non-zero. Qdrant and its volume are never touched in any path. Clean up the mktemp dir on exit; keep the backups.

2. .github/workflows/chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml — add operations `octopus-upgrade-preflight` and `octopus-upgrade-apply` to the choice list and the request allowlist; `octopus-upgrade-apply` requires `workflow_dispatch` on `refs/heads/main` exactly like `v3-host-cleanup`. No new secrets, no change to host-key handling, no caller-controlled values reach the host.
